newsitem.title: UK: Euro VGO steady, arb to U.S tightens, demand slows.
newsitem.headline: Euro VGO steady, arb to U.S tightens, demand slows.

text.p: Expectations of Russian vacuum gas oil supplies coming into Europe, slower U.S. demand and jittery crude prices have kept prices broadly steady. Low Rhine levels restricting barge movements to around 1,000 tonnes was causing logistical difficulties and higher freight charges.
A 15,000 tonne low sulphur parcel was sold into Germany on Wednesday at quotes plus a premium for delivery during October.

Dealers said demand in NWE was drying up and that any boost will have to come from the U.S. The transatlantic arb, which has been very open, has narrowed and sellers holding for high prices given crude's recovery today may end up with distressed cargoes.
A low sulphur VGO cargo out of Scandanavia was available for Oct 1-4 loading, but no firm price offer was heard.
